item.title: 1972: Former NL Batting Champion Matty Alou Is Traded by the Oakland
item.description: Former NL batting champion Matty Alou is traded by the Oakland Athletics to the New York Yankees for pitcher Rob Gardner and infielder Rich McKinney ("PTBNL"). Alou, 33, starred in the 1972 ALCS but went only 1-for-24 (.042) in seven games during Oakland's 1972 World Series triumph. Photo: St. Louis Cardinals / Major League Baseball (Public domain).

item.title: 2023: Amézaga Was Named Manager of the Saraperos De Saltillo of the Mexican
item.description: On November 24, 2023, Amézaga was named manager of the Saraperos de Saltillo of the Mexican League for the 2024 season. Photo: User Chrisjnelson on en.wikipedia (Public domain).

item.title: 2015: Bobby Smith, 81, Backup Outfielder for the St. Louis Cardinals
item.description: Bobby Smith, 81, backup outfielder for the St. Louis Cardinals, Philadelphia Phillies, New York Mets, Chicago Cubs and Los Angeles Angels in parts of seven seasons spanning 1957–1965.

item.title: 2012: Following the 2012 Season, on November 24, 2012, Hale Was Named
item.description: Following the 2012 season, on November 24, 2012, Hale was named as the new bench coach for the Toronto Blue Jays, replacing Don Wakamatsu. Photo: Keith Allison from Owings Mills, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2010: Leyva Was Named the Pittsburgh Pirates' Third Base Coach
item.description: On November 24, 2010, Leyva was named the Pittsburgh Pirates' third base coach, under new manager Clint Hurdle. Photo: Johnmaxmena (talk)john Mena (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 2010: A. Arthur Giddon, 101, Lawyer and World War II Veteran, Who Served
item.description: A. Arthur Giddon, 101, lawyer and World War II veteran, who served as a 13-year-old batboy for the 1922 Boston Braves.

item.title: 2009: Albert Pujols of the St. Louis Cardinals Receives His Third National
item.description: Albert Pujols of the St. Louis Cardinals receives his third National League MVP Award, tying eight others who also had three. Only Barry Bonds has more with seven. Pujols, who also won in 2005 and 2008, receives all 32 first-place votes and 448 points in balloting announced by the BBWAA. Florida's Hanley Ramírez, the NL batting champion, is second with 233 points, followed by Philadelphia's Ryan Howard (217) and… Photo: Jim Accordino at https://www.flickr.com/photos/jimmyack205/ (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2006: Lee Agreed to a Six-Year, $100 Million Contract
item.description: On November 24, 2006, Lee agreed to a six-year, $100 million contract with the Houston Astros. Photo: SBoyd (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2005: On Thanksgiving Evening, the Boston Red Sox Officially Announce
item.description: On Thanksgiving evening, the Boston Red Sox officially announce the acquisition of pitcher Josh Beckett and third baseman Mike Lowell from the Florida Marlins. Boston also add reliever Guillermo Mota in the deal, while sending minor league prospects shortstop Hanley Ramírez and pitchers Aníbal Sánchez, Jesús Delgado and Harvey García to the Marlins. Photo: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2003: Warren Spahn, 82, Hall of Fame Pitcher for the Boston/Milwaukee
item.description: Warren Spahn, 82, Hall of Fame pitcher for the Boston/Milwaukee Braves (1942, 1946–1964), New York Mets (1965) and San Francisco Giants (1965), whose 363 career victories made him the fifth-winningest pitcher – and the winningest left-hander – in MLB history; compiled thirteen 20-win seasons, including Cy Young Award campaign in 1957 World Series championship season, 14 All-Star Game appearances and two no-hitters… Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1991: Carl Sawatski, 64, Catcher and Pinch Hitter for the Chicago Cubs
item.description: Carl Sawatski, 64, catcher and pinch hitter for the Chicago Cubs, Chicago White Sox, Milwaukee Braves, Philadelphia Phillies and St. Louis Cardinals between 1954 and 1963, who helped the Braves win the 1957 World Series and the 1958 National League pennant; longtime and influential minor-league executive. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1989: The Texas Rangers Sign Four-Time Gold Glove Center-Fielder Gary
item.description: The Texas Rangers sign four-time Gold Glove center-fielder Gary Pettis, granted free agency on November 13 from the Detroit Tigers. Photo: oaktree_brian_1976 (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1986: St. Louis Cardinals Reliever Todd Worrell
item.description: St. Louis Cardinals reliever Todd Worrell, who led the National League with 36 saves, receives Rookie of the Year honors. Worrell had helped St. Louis to the 1985 World Series as a late-season call-up but was still a rookie in 1986, as defined by the BBWAA. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1982: Cal Ripken Jr., Who Hit .264 With 28 Home Runs and 93 RBI
item.description: Cal Ripken Jr., who hit .264 with 28 home runs and 93 RBI as a shortstop and third baseman for the Baltimore Orioles, is named American League Rookie of the Year. Ripken gets 24 of 28 first place votes, with the others going to Kent Hrbek of the Minnesota Twins. Photo: Maryland GovPics (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1976: Franks Returned to the Major Leagues
item.description: Franks returned to the major leagues as newly appointed Cubs general manager Bob Kennedy's first and only choice to replace Jim Marshall as manager on November 24, 1976. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1971: Catcher-Infielder Earl Williams, Who Hit 33 Home Runs
item.description: Catcher-infielder Earl Williams, who hit 33 home runs and 87 RBI for the Atlanta Braves, wins the National League Rookie of the Year honors. Williams gets 18 of 24 first place votes, with the others going to Willie Montañez of the Philadelphia Phillies. Photo: Hostess (Public domain).

item.title: 1969: A Busy Offseason of Managerial Changes in the American League
item.description: A busy offseason of managerial changes in the American League concludes when Dave Bristol, fired by the Cincinnati Reds in October, replaces Joe Schultz at the helm of the Seattle Pilots; earlier, Eddie Kasko was named Dick Williams' permanent successor with the Boston Red Sox (October 2); Charlie Metro replaced Joe Gordon with the Kansas City Royals (October 8); and Bill Rigney, dismissed by the California Angels… Photo: Atlanta Braves (Public domain).

item.title: 1964: St. Louis Cardinals Third Baseman Ken Boyer, Who Hit .295
item.description: St. Louis Cardinals third baseman Ken Boyer, who hit .295 with 24 home runs and 119 RBI, is named the NL's Most Valuable Player with 14 first-place votes and 243 points, becoming the first Redbird MVP since Stan Musial won his third award in 1948. Johnny Callison (two votes, 187 points) and Boyer's teammate Bill White (two, 106) are the runners-up. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1953: After What The New York Times Calls a Month-Long "Guessing Game,"
item.description: After what The New York Times calls a month-long "guessing game," the Brooklyn Dodgers sign Walter Alston, 42, a veteran minor-league manager, to a one-year pact to lead their team on the field in 1954. Although he has fashioned an outstanding record in Brooklyn's farm system, most recently with the Triple-A St. Paul Saints and Montreal Royals, Alston is so obscure a choice compared to well-known figures such as Pee… Photo: UPI (Public domain).

item.title: 1951: The St. Louis Cardinals Fire Manager Marty Marion
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals fire manager Marty Marion after only one season at the team's helm. Eight-time NL All-Star shortstop Marion, 33, led the 1951 Redbirds to an 81–73 mark and third-place finish. Photo: Bowman Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 1942: The St. Louis Cardinals Select Right-Hander Gerry Staley From Boise
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals select right-hander Gerry Staley from Boise of the Class C Pioneer League in the minor league draft. In 1947, Staley will begin a 15-season MLB career during which he makes four All-Star teams and wins 134 games, including 89 as a Cardinal. Photo: Bowman Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 1941: A Week Before Minor League Baseball's Annual Meetings
item.description: A week before minor league baseball's annual meetings, the International League comes to the aid of a flagship club, the Toronto Maple Leafs. A charter member of the IL that's played continuously since 1895, the Leafs have recently struggled in the standings and at the gate, play no Sunday home games due to local blue laws, and have been sold to new owners who've pledged to keep the team alive.

item.title: 1887: George Hancock Invents an Indoor Baseball Game That Would Become
item.description: George Hancock invents an indoor baseball game that would become known as softball in Chicago. Photo: LauraHale (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1883: The American Association Agree to Expand to 12 Teams by Admitting
item.description: The American Association agree to expand to 12 teams by admitting the Brooklyn Atlantics, Indianapolis Hoosiers, Toledo Blue Stockings and Washington Nationals. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1879: Taking Advantage of the New Reserve Rule
item.description: Taking advantage of the new reserve rule, the Providence Grays offer reserved player-manager George Wright a 15 percent pay cut from his $2,000 salary, after he guided the Grays to the pennant. Wright refuses and, as a named reserve player, will receive no offers from any other National League club. Photo: George Kendall Warren (Public domain).

item.title: 1877: The New York Mercury Prints an Amazingly Accurate Prediction About
item.description: The New York Mercury prints an amazingly accurate prediction about the future of baseball. "The baseball mania is getting so bad that every city will soon have a mammoth structure like the Roman Coliseum to play in. This will be illuminated by electric lights so that games can be played nights‚ thus overcoming a serious objection at present existing."
